q: The chemical compounds found in living things are referred to as "____" due to their link with organisms.
e: The chemical compounds found in living things are referred to as "organic compounds" due to their link with organisms. Organic compounds are the carbon compounds linked to living things.

q: The simplest organic compounds that contain only the elements carbon and hydrogen are called ____.
e: The simplest organic compounds that contain only the elements carbon and hydrogen are called hydrocarbons. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen.

q: Ethers can be used as organic solvents in the perfumery and ____ industries.
e: Ethers can be used as organic solvents in the perfumery and aroma industries. Aroma is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Carboxylic acids are present in many common household items such as vinegar (____ acid).
e: Carboxylic acids are present in many common household items such as vinegar (acetic acid). Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Some other organic compounds contain nitrogen atoms, such as amines and ____.
e: Some other organic compounds contain nitrogen atoms, such as amines and amides. Amides is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: An ether is an organic compound with an O atom bonded to two ____ groups.
e: An ether is an organic compound with an O atom bonded to two alkyl groups. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: In a symmetrical ether, the two alkyl groups are the ____.
e: In a symmetrical ether, the two alkyl groups are the same. Equal forward and reverse rates keep concentrations the same at equilibrium.

q: Ethers have the general formula ____.
e: Ethers have the general formula CnH2n+2O. CnH2n+2O is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the IUPAC system, the oxygen atom and the smaller alkyl group are named as an ____ substituent.
e: In the IUPAC system, the oxygen atom and the smaller alkyl group are named as an alkoxy substituent. Alkoxy is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ethers can be obtained from alcohol by the elimination of a molecule of ____ from two molecules of alcohol.
e: Ethers can be obtained from alcohol by the elimination of a molecule of water from two molecules of alcohol. Water is often the solvent, the proton host, or a condensation product, depending on the stem.

q: There is no intermolecular ____ bonding between ether molecules, which makes their boiling points much lower than alcohol of similar molecular mass.
e: There is no intermolecular hydrogen bonding between ether molecules, which makes their boiling points much lower than alcohol of similar molecular mass. Hydrogen here is the element or the proton being transferred in the chemistry of this stem.

q: On heating with concentrated hydrogen iodide (HI), the C-O bond in ethers breaks forming alcohol and ____.
e: On heating with concentrated hydrogen iodide (HI), the C-O bond in ethers breaks forming alcohol and alkyl iodide. Alkyl iodide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ethoxyethane (diethyl ether), the most common member of the ether family, was used for many years as a surgical ____ agent.
e: Ethoxyethane (diethyl ether), the most common member of the ether family, was used for many years as a surgical anaesthetic agent. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: Aldehydes and ketones are organic compounds which contain the ____ group, >C=O.
e: Aldehydes and ketones are organic compounds which contain the carbonyl group, >C=O. Carbonyl is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In aldehydes, a carbonyl group located at the end of a carbon chain is bonded to at least one ____ atom.
e: In aldehydes, a carbonyl group located at the end of a carbon chain is bonded to at least one hydrogen atom. Hydrogen here is the element or the proton being transferred in the chemistry of this stem.

q: Aldehydes and ketones have the general formula ____.
e: Aldehydes and ketones have the general formula CnH2nO. CnH2nO is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The common names of aldehydes are given based on the names of corresponding ____ acids.
e: The common names of aldehydes are given based on the names of corresponding carboxylic acids. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: An alpha ($\alpha$) carbon is a carbon atom bonded to a ____ group.
e: An alpha () carbon is a carbon atom bonded to a functional group. The functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the organic family.

q: The systematic (IUPAC) names are derived from the names of the parent ____.
e: The systematic (IUPAC) names are derived from the names of the parent hydrocarbons. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen.

q: The suffix ____ instead of e is added to the characteristic stem for aldehydes.
e: The suffix -al instead of e is added to the characteristic stem for aldehydes. -al is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Primary and secondary alcohols give aldehydes and ____, respectively, when oxidised.
e: Primary and secondary alcohols give aldehydes and ketones, respectively, when oxidised. In a secondary alcohol the carbon that holds OH is attached to two other carbons.

q: The aldehyde product is obtained by ____ to remove it immediately from the reaction mixture.
e: The aldehyde product is obtained by distillation to remove it immediately from the reaction mixture. Aldehydes have a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: The addition of water to ethyne in the presence of $H_2SO_4$ and ____ produces ethanal.
e: The addition of water to ethyne in the presence of H2SO4 and HgSO4 produces ethanal. HgSO4 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to ____ acids with common oxidising agents.
e: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to carboxylic acids with common oxidising agents. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Aldehydes and ketones are easily reduced to the corresponding primary and secondary alcohols, using the reducing agent lithium aluminium hydride, ____.
e: Aldehydes and ketones are easily reduced to the corresponding primary and secondary alcohols, using the reducing agent lithium aluminium hydride, LiAlH4. In a secondary alcohol the carbon that holds OH is attached to two other carbons.

q: Hydrogen cyanide, HCN, adds across the carbon-oxygen double bond in aldehydes and some ketones to produce compounds known as ____.
e: Hydrogen cyanide, HCN, adds across the carbon-oxygen double bond in aldehydes and some ketones to produce compounds known as hydroxynitriles. Hydroxynitriles is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Formalin (40% aqueous solution of methanal) is used as a disinfectant and a preservative for biological ____.
e: Formalin (40% aqueous solution of methanal) is used as a disinfectant and a preservative for biological specimens. Specimens is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ketones are popular solvents for other moderately polar substances, including waxes, plastics, paints, lacquers, varnishes, and ____.
e: Ketones are popular solvents for other moderately polar substances, including waxes, plastics, paints, lacquers, varnishes, and glues. Glues is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Carboxylic acids are organic compounds with a carboxyl functional group ____.
e: Carboxylic acids are organic compounds with a carboxyl functional group -COOH. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: The carboxyl group is made up of a carbonyl group and a ____ group.
e: The carboxyl group is made up of a carbonyl group and a hydroxyl group. Hydroxyl is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Formic acid was obtained by distillation of ants (Latin formica, meaning "____").
e: Formic acid was obtained by distillation of ants (Latin formica, meaning "ant"). Ant is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Since a carboxylic acid group must always be found at the end of a carbon chain, it is always given the "____" location position in numbering.
e: Since a carboxylic acid group must always be found at the end of a carbon chain, it is always given the "1" location position in numbering. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Ethanoic acid is formed by the oxidation of ____.
e: Ethanoic acid is formed by the oxidation of ethanol. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: Instead of a distillation set, a ____ condenser has to be used so that the volatile components remain in the reaction for long enough to complete their reaction.
e: Instead of a distillation set, a reflux condenser has to be used so that the volatile components remain in the reaction for long enough to complete their reaction. Reflux is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ethanol is oxidised by atmospheric oxygen in the presence of bacteria (____).
e: Ethanol is oxidised by atmospheric oxygen in the presence of bacteria (Acetobacter). Acetobacter is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Carboxylic acids are weak acids, and they can react with reactive metals such as sodium, potassium, and magnesium to give salt and ____.
e: Carboxylic acids are weak acids, and they can react with reactive metals such as sodium, potassium, and magnesium to give salt and hydrogen. Hydrogen here is the element or the proton being transferred in the chemistry of this stem.

q: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to give salt, water and ____.
e: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to give salt, water and carbon dioxide. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Carboxylic acids are reduced to their corresponding primary alcohols using the reducing agent, $LiAlH_4$, in dry ____ at room temperature.
e: Carboxylic acids are reduced to their corresponding primary alcohols using the reducing agent, LiAlH4, in dry ether at room temperature. In a primary alcohol the carbon that holds OH is attached to only one other carbon, or it is CH3OH.

q: The popular painkiller, aspirin, is the acetyl derivative of ____ acid.
e: The popular painkiller, aspirin, is the acetyl derivative of salicylic acid. Salicylic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Esters are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the hydroxyl (-OH) group has been replaced by an ____ (-OR) group.
e: Esters are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the hydroxyl (-OH) group has been replaced by an alkoxy (-OR) group. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Generally, carboxylic acid can react with alcohol to form ester in a process which is known as ____.
e: Generally, carboxylic acid can react with alcohol to form ester in a process which is known as esterification. Esterification is the reaction of an alcohol with an acid to make an ester and water.

q: Acidic hydrolysis is simply the reverse of ____.
e: Acidic hydrolysis is simply the reverse of esterification. Esterification is the reaction of an alcohol with an acid to make an ester and water.

q: When an ester is refluxed with an alkali, such as aqueous sodium hydroxide, it is fully ____.
e: When an ester is refluxed with an alkali, such as aqueous sodium hydroxide, it is fully hydrolysed. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: The most common method of transesterification is the reaction of the ester with an alcohol in the presence of an acid ____.
e: The most common method of transesterification is the reaction of the ester with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst. The catalyst changes rate without being consumed in the overall equation.

q: Naturally-occurring esters (animal fats or vegetable oil) mixed with NaOH produce ____ that is used for washing dishes and clothes.
e: Naturally-occurring esters (animal fats or vegetable oil) mixed with NaOH produce soap that is used for washing dishes and clothes. Soap is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: An amine is a compound in which one or more hydrogen atoms of ammonia have been replaced by ____ groups.
e: An amine is a compound in which one or more hydrogen atoms of ammonia have been replaced by alkyl groups. Alkyl: amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Amines are classified as primary ($1^\circ$), secondary ($2^\circ$), and tertiary ($3^\circ$), depending on how many alkyl groups are attached to the ____.
e: Amines are classified as primary (1degrees), secondary (2degrees), and tertiary (3degrees), depending on how many alkyl groups are attached to the nitrogen. Nitrogen is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ethanamine is prepared by heating bromoethane with an excess of ammonia dissolved in ____ in a sealed tube.
e: Ethanamine is prepared by heating bromoethane with an excess of ammonia dissolved in ethanol in a sealed tube. Ethanol is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Because more hydrogen bonds are formed in primary amines, they are more soluble in water than secondary and ____ amines.
e: Because more hydrogen bonds are formed in primary amines, they are more soluble in water than secondary and tertiary amines. A hydrogen bond is the strong intermolecular pull from H attached to N, O, or F toward another N, O, or F.

q: Ethanamine reacts with chloroform in the presence of an alkali to form ethyl isocyanide with an unpleasant smell; this reaction is known as ____ reaction.
e: Ethanamine reacts with chloroform in the presence of an alkali to form ethyl isocyanide with an unpleasant smell; this reaction is known as carbylamine reaction. Carbylamine is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Amides are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the -OH of the carboxylic acid has been replaced by $-NH_2$, -NHR, or ____ of an amine.
e: Amides are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the -OH of the carboxylic acid has been replaced by -NH2, -NHR, or -NR2 of an amine. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: The addition of ammonia ($NH_3$) to a carboxylic acid forms an amide via a ____ reaction.
e: The addition of ammonia (NH3) to a carboxylic acid forms an amide via a condensation reaction. Condensation joins molecules and knocks out water or another small molecule.

q: Generally, amides can be hydrolysed in either acidic or ____ solutions.
e: Generally, amides can be hydrolysed in either acidic or basic solutions. Basic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The groups of atoms that are attached to the carbon backbone of organic compounds are known as ____ groups.
e: The groups of atoms that are attached to the carbon backbone of organic compounds are known as functional groups. The functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the organic family.

q: The most important common techniques are infrared (IR), ultraviolet/visible (UV/Vis), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and ____ spectrometry.
e: The most important common techniques are infrared (IR), ultraviolet/visible (UV/Vis), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and mass spectrometry. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: A chemical test is typically a fast reaction performed in a test tube that gives a visual clue (a colour change, precipitate, or ____ formation).
e: A chemical test is typically a fast reaction performed in a test tube that gives a visual clue (a colour change, precipitate, or gas formation). Gas is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Alkenes mixed with 1% $KMnO_4$ solution result in ____.
e: Alkenes mixed with 1% KMnO4 solution result in decolourisation. Decolourisation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Alkynes passed through ammoniacal $Cu_2Cl_2$ solution give a ____ coloured precipitate.
e: Alkynes passed through ammoniacal Cu2Cl2 solution give a red coloured precipitate. Red is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Alcohols warmed with acidified $K_2Cr_2O_7$ solution change from orange colour to ____ colour.
e: Alcohols warmed with acidified K2Cr2O7 solution change from orange colour to green colour. Green is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Aldehydes heated gently with Fehling's solution give a ____ coloured precipitate.
e: Aldehydes heated gently with Fehling's solution give a reddish-brown coloured precipitate. Reddish-brown is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ketones mixed with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP) solution give a deep-____ coloured precipitate.
e: Ketones mixed with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP) solution give a deep-orange coloured precipitate. Orange is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Carboxylic acids mixed with saturated $NaHCO_3$ solution result in the evolution of ____.
e: Carboxylic acids mixed with saturated NaHCO3 solution result in the evolution of CO2. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Primary amines reacted with $CHCl_3$ in the presence of alkali produce an unpleasant ____.
e: Primary amines reacted with CHCl3 in the presence of alkali produce an unpleasant smell. Smell is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The presence of a carbonyl group such as aldehyde or ketone can be easily tested by using a solution of ____.
e: The presence of a carbonyl group such as aldehyde or ketone can be easily tested by using a solution of 2,4-DNP. Aldehydes have a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Fehling's solution is an alkaline solution containing copper(____) ions.
e: Fehling's solution is an alkaline solution containing copper(II) ions. II is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Infrared (IR) spectroscopy is the study of the absorption of light by a compound, in the ____ region of electromagnetic spectrum.
e: Infrared (IR) spectroscopy is the study of the absorption of light by a compound, in the infrared region of electromagnetic spectrum. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: The relationship between the energy (E) and the frequency ($\nu$) or wavelength ($\lambda$) of the electromagnetic radiation is described by ____'s equation.
e: The relationship between the energy (E) and the frequency () or wavelength () of the electromagnetic radiation is described by Planck's equation. Wavelength is the distance from one wave crest to the next.

q: Wavenumber (measured in $cm^{-1}$) which is the reciprocal of the ____, is one way to describe the frequency of electromagnetic radiation.
e: Wavenumber (measured in cm-1) which is the reciprocal of the wavelength, is one way to describe the frequency of electromagnetic radiation. Wavenumber counts how many waves fit into one centimetre.

q: Stretching is a vibration that occurs along the bond line and changes the bond ____.
e: Stretching is a vibration that occurs along the bond line and changes the bond length. Length is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Bending is a vibration that occurs between two bonds and changes the bond ____.
e: Bending is a vibration that occurs between two bonds and changes the bond angle. Angle is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Only those stretching and bending motions that change the ____ moment of a molecule give rise to the absorption of infrared radiation.
e: Only those stretching and bending motions that change the dipole moment of a molecule give rise to the absorption of infrared radiation. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: Light atoms, for example, vibrate at higher frequencies than heavier atoms and multiple bonds vibrate at higher frequencies than ____ bonds.
e: Light atoms, for example, vibrate at higher frequencies than heavier atoms and multiple bonds vibrate at higher frequencies than single bonds. Single is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The instrument used to obtain an infrared spectrum is called an IR ____.
e: The instrument used to obtain an infrared spectrum is called an IR spectrometer. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: The presence of hydrogen bonds in molecules also affects the ____ of the absorption bands.
e: The presence of hydrogen bonds in molecules also affects the shape of the absorption bands. A hydrogen bond is the strong intermolecular pull from H attached to N, O, or F toward another N, O, or F.

q: The OH bond of alcohols usually has an absorption in the range of 3200-3600 $cm^{-1}$, while the OH bond of carboxylic acids occurs in the range of ____ $cm^{-1}$.
e: The OH bond of alcohols usually has an absorption in the range of 3200-3600 cm-1, while the OH bond of carboxylic acids occurs in the range of 2500-3300 cm-1. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: An alkane lacks functional groups whereas an alkene and an alkyne have functional groups which are carbon-carbon double bond and carbon-carbon ____ bond, respectively.
e: An alkane lacks functional groups whereas an alkene and an alkyne have functional groups which are carbon-carbon double bond and carbon-carbon triple bond, respectively. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: The most common functional groups in organic compounds other than hydrocarbons are carbonyl (C=O), hydroxyl (OH), carboxyl (COOH), carboalkoxy (COOR), amine ($NH_2$) and carboxamide (____).
e: The most common functional groups in organic compounds other than hydrocarbons are carbonyl (C=O), hydroxyl (OH), carboxyl (COOH), carboalkoxy (COOR), amine (NH2) and carboxamide (CONH2). A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: The identification of the organic compound is based on simple chemical tests and ____ techniques that indicate the presence of specific functional groups.
e: The identification of the organic compound is based on simple chemical tests and spectroscopic techniques that indicate the presence of specific functional groups. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: Alkanes mixed with 1% $KMnO_4$ solution show no ____.
e: Alkanes mixed with 1% KMnO4 solution show no decolourisation. Decolourisation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ethers boiled with HI and then reacted with $AgNO_3$ give a ____ coloured precipitate.
e: Ethers boiled with HI and then reacted with AgNO3 give a yellow coloured precipitate. Yellow is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Primary amides boiled with 20% NaOH solution result in the evolution of ____.
e: Primary amides boiled with 20% NaOH solution result in the evolution of NH3. NH3 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Fehling's solution can be used to distinguish aldehyde and ketone functional groups because aldehydes can be further oxidised to form carboxylic acids, but ketones cannot be oxidised ____.
e: Fehling's solution can be used to distinguish aldehyde and ketone functional groups because aldehydes can be further oxidised to form carboxylic acids, but ketones cannot be oxidised easily. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: When the clear blue Fehling's solution is warmed with an aldehyde, the reddish-brown precipitate of ____ is formed.
e: When the clear blue Fehling's solution is warmed with an aldehyde, the reddish-brown precipitate of Cu2O is formed. Aldehydes have a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Chemical tests are handy but not always practical for the identification of compounds with complex ____.
e: Chemical tests are handy but not always practical for the identification of compounds with complex structures. Structures is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The spectroscopic techniques can be performed quickly on small amounts of a compound and can provide much more information about the compound's ____.
e: The spectroscopic techniques can be performed quickly on small amounts of a compound and can provide much more information about the compound's structure. Structure is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Additionally, spectroscopic techniques are also non-____ techniques compared to methods using chemical reactions.
e: Additionally, spectroscopic techniques are also non-destructive techniques compared to methods using chemical reactions. Destructive is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Because electromagnetic radiation has wave-like properties, it is characterised by either its frequency or its ____.
e: Because electromagnetic radiation has wave-like properties, it is characterised by either its frequency or its wavelength. Wavelength is the distance from one wave crest to the next.

q: High frequencies, large wavenumbers, and short wavelengths are associated with high ____.
e: High frequencies, large wavenumbers, and short wavelengths are associated with high energies. Energies is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Photons in the infrared radiation region can cause bond ____ in molecules.
e: Photons in the infrared radiation region can cause bond vibrations in molecules. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: The frequency of the absorbed radiation matches the frequency of the bond or group that ____.
e: The frequency of the absorbed radiation matches the frequency of the bond or group that vibrates. Frequency is how many wave crests pass a point each second.

q: Homonuclear diatomic molecules (e.g., $N_2$) which have no dipole moments are IR ____.
e: Homonuclear diatomic molecules (e.g., N2) which have no dipole moments are IR inactive. Dipole moment measures how polar a bond or molecule is.

q: On the other hand, heteronuclear diatomic molecules (e.g., CO) which have dipole moments are IR ____.
e: On the other hand, heteronuclear diatomic molecules (e.g., CO) which have dipole moments are IR active. Dipole moment measures how polar a bond or molecule is.

q: Each stretching and bending vibration occurs with a characteristic frequency which depends on the bond strength and the ____ of the atoms.
e: Each stretching and bending vibration occurs with a characteristic frequency which depends on the bond strength and the masses of the atoms. Frequency is how many wave crests pass a point each second.

q: It takes more energy to stretch a bond than to ____ it.
e: It takes more energy to stretch a bond than to bend it. Bend is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: When a sample is irradiated with electromagnetic radiation in the infrared region, an IR spectrum is obtained as a plot of the percent transmittance or absorbance of radiation versus the ____ of the radiation transmitted.
e: When a sample is irradiated with electromagnetic radiation in the infrared region, an IR spectrum is obtained as a plot of the percent transmittance or absorbance of radiation versus the wavenumber of the radiation transmitted. Wavenumber counts how many waves fit into one centimetre.

q: Different functional groups produce bond absorptions at different locations and ____ on the IR spectrum.
e: Different functional groups produce bond absorptions at different locations and intensities on the IR spectrum. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: The important factors that influence the intensity of an absorption band are polarity of the bond and number of ____.
e: The important factors that influence the intensity of an absorption band are polarity of the bond and number of bonds. Bonds is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The higher bond polarity and more number of bonds in molecules will give a more intense absorption ____.
e: The higher bond polarity and more number of bonds in molecules will give a more intense absorption band. Band is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The broad shape of the absorption band for O-H results from the hydrogen bonding of the OH groups between ____.
e: The broad shape of the absorption band for O-H results from the hydrogen bonding of the OH groups between molecules. A hydrogen bond is the strong intermolecular pull from H attached to N, O, or F toward another N, O, or F.

q: Consider N-H stretches in amine and amide which are medium intensity and width compared to O-H stretches; N-H stretch is narrow and weak while the O-H stretch is broad and ____.
e: Consider N-H stretches in amine and amide which are medium intensity and width compared to O-H stretches; N-H stretch is narrow and weak while the O-H stretch is broad and strong. Amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: A macromolecule is a very large molecule that contains thousands of atoms or more, because "____" means large.
e: A macromolecule is a very large molecule that contains thousands of atoms or more, because "macro" means large. Macro is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Carbohydrates (starch, cellulose), proteins and natural fibres (____) are found in nature.
e: Carbohydrates (starch, cellulose), proteins and natural fibres (cotton) are found in nature. Cotton is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A polymer is a type of long-chain macromolecule that is linked together by many small repeat units known as ____.
e: A polymer is a type of long-chain macromolecule that is linked together by many small repeat units known as monomers. Monomers are the small repeating starting molecules of a polymer.

q: If a polymer consists of only one kind of monomers then it is called a ____.
e: If a polymer consists of only one kind of monomers then it is called a homopolymer. A homopolymer is built from only one kind of monomer.

q: When a polymer is made, monomers bond together one after another in a rapid series of steps; the process of joining together a large number of monomers to form a polymer is called ____.
e: When a polymer is made, monomers bond together one after another in a rapid series of steps; the process of joining together a large number of monomers to form a polymer is called polymerisation. A polymer is a giant molecule made by linking many small monomer units.

q: Addition polymerisation occurs when unsaturated monomers join together without losing any molecules or ____.
e: Addition polymerisation occurs when unsaturated monomers join together without losing any molecules or atoms. Addition polymerisation joins monomers that have C=C double bonds without losing a small molecule.

q: Condensation polymerisation occurs when the monomers combine to form a polymer, with the removal of a small molecule such as ____.
e: Condensation polymerisation occurs when the monomers combine to form a polymer, with the removal of a small molecule such as water. Water is often the solvent, the proton host, or a condensation product, depending on the stem.

q: The simplest addition polymer is polyethene or polyethylene (____).
e: The simplest addition polymer is polyethene or polyethylene (PE). A polymer is a giant molecule made by linking many small monomer units.

q: At high temperature and pressure, and in the presence of a ____, the carbon-carbon double bonds of the ethene molecules break.
e: At high temperature and pressure, and in the presence of a catalyst, the carbon-carbon double bonds of the ethene molecules break. The catalyst changes rate without being consumed in the overall equation.

q: The number of ethene molecules in each polyethene molecule varies from 10,000 to ____.
e: The number of ethene molecules in each polyethene molecule varies from 10,000 to 30,000. 30,000 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Another example of an addition polymer is polychloroethene or polyvinyl chloride (____).
e: Another example of an addition polymer is polychloroethene or polyvinyl chloride (PVC). A polymer is a giant molecule made by linking many small monomer units.

q: In polyalkenes made of one type of monomer, the repeat unit is the same as the monomer except that the carbon-carbon double bond (C=C) is changed to a carbon-carbon ____ bond.
e: In polyalkenes made of one type of monomer, the repeat unit is the same as the monomer except that the carbon-carbon double bond (C=C) is changed to a carbon-carbon single bond. A monomer is a small reactive molecule that joins again and again to build a polymer.

q: Addition polymers are sometimes referred to as ____.
e: Addition polymers are sometimes referred to as plastics. Plastics is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: At low temperatures, plastics lose plasticity and elasticity and become ____.
e: At low temperatures, plastics lose plasticity and elasticity and become brittle. Brittle is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Many frying pans are coated with a layer of teflon, which is heat-resistant and has ____ properties.
e: Many frying pans are coated with a layer of teflon, which is heat-resistant and has non-stick properties. Non-stick is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Polystyrene is hard, light and ____.
e: Polystyrene is hard, light and brittle. Brittle is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Condensation polymers are polymers whose process of polymerisation involves a ____ reaction.
e: Condensation polymers are polymers whose process of polymerisation involves a condensation reaction. Condensation joins molecules and knocks out water or another small molecule.

q: Condensation polymerisation is characterised by monomers that contain two different ____ groups.
e: Condensation polymerisation is characterised by monomers that contain two different functional groups. The functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the organic family.

q: Terylene or polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is formed from the reaction of an acid monomer (terephthalic acid) and an alcohol monomer (____).
e: Terylene or polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is formed from the reaction of an acid monomer (terephthalic acid) and an alcohol monomer (ethylene glycol). A monomer is a small reactive molecule that joins again and again to build a polymer.

q: In the condensation polymerisation process, a hydrogen atom is lost from the alcohol, and a ____ group is lost from the carboxylic acid.
e: In the condensation polymerisation process, a hydrogen atom is lost from the alcohol, and a hydroxyl group is lost from the carboxylic acid. Condensation polymerisation joins monomers and knocks out a small molecule such as water.

q: Terylene is polyester as it contains many ____ linkages.
e: Terylene is polyester as it contains many ester linkages. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: Nylon is an example of polyamides, made from a dicarboxylic acid and a ____.
e: Nylon is an example of polyamides, made from a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine. Diamine is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Nylon 6,6 is formed from the reaction of an acid monomer (adipic acid) and an amine monomer (1,6-____).
e: Nylon 6,6 is formed from the reaction of an acid monomer (adipic acid) and an amine monomer (1,6-diaminohexane). A monomer is a small reactive molecule that joins again and again to build a polymer.

q: A new bond is formed between nitrogen and carbon atoms to form an ____ linkage.
e: A new bond is formed between nitrogen and carbon atoms to form an amide linkage. Amide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A large protein molecule is one of the types of ____.
e: A large protein molecule is one of the types of polyamides. Polyamides is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Proteins are made from thousands of amino acid ____.
e: Proteins are made from thousands of amino acid monomers. Monomers are the small repeating starting molecules of a polymer.

q: The general formula of amino acid is ____.
e: The general formula of amino acid is H2NCHRCOOH. H2NCHRCOOH is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The covalent bond formed between two amino acids is called a ____ bond.
e: The covalent bond formed between two amino acids is called a peptide bond. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: Condensation polymers often have lower molecular masses than ____ polymers.
e: Condensation polymers often have lower molecular masses than addition polymers. Addition is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The presence of polar functional groups on the chains often enhances chain-chain attractions, particularly if ____ bonding is involved.
e: The presence of polar functional groups on the chains often enhances chain-chain attractions, particularly if hydrogen bonding is involved. Hydrogen here is the element or the proton being transferred in the chemistry of this stem.

q: Terylene is resistant to stretching and ____.
e: Terylene is resistant to stretching and shrinking. Shrinking is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Nylon is very strong and resistant, and is used in fishing line, shoes, toothbrush bristles, guitar strings and machine ____.
e: Nylon is very strong and resistant, and is used in fishing line, shoes, toothbrush bristles, guitar strings and machine parts. Parts is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Plastics are particular types of polymers that can be ____.
e: Plastics are particular types of polymers that can be moulded. Moulded is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Since plastics are relatively cheap, easily moulded, light, tough, waterproof and are resistant to decay, rusting and chemical attack, they are non-____.
e: Since plastics are relatively cheap, easily moulded, light, tough, waterproof and are resistant to decay, rusting and chemical attack, they are non-biodegradable. Biodegradable plastics can be broken down by microorganisms.

q: PVC produces corrosive hydrogen ____ gas during combustion.
e: PVC produces corrosive hydrogen chloride gas during combustion. Chloride is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Plastics that are thrown into the sea endanger ____ animals.
e: Plastics that are thrown into the sea endanger marine animals. Marine is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: When plastic waste is buried in a landfill, it can remain there for hundreds of years, contaminating the ____.
e: When plastic waste is buried in a landfill, it can remain there for hundreds of years, contaminating the soil. Soil is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: To aid in the separation, manufacturers require to place a recycling ____ on their products to indicate the type of plastic it is.
e: To aid in the separation, manufacturers require to place a recycling symbol on their products to indicate the type of plastic it is. Symbol is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The lower the number in the middle of the recycling symbol, the greater is the ease with which the material can be ____.
e: The lower the number in the middle of the recycling symbol, the greater is the ease with which the material can be recycled. Recycled is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: PETE/PET stands for polyethylene ____.
e: PETE/PET stands for polyethylene terephthalate. Terephthalate is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: HDPE stands for high-density ____.
e: HDPE stands for high-density polyethylene. Polyethylene is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Biodegradable plastics are made from monomers derived directly from plant materials, such as polylactic acid (____).
e: Biodegradable plastics are made from monomers derived directly from plant materials, such as polylactic acid (PLA). Biodegradable plastics can be broken down by microorganisms.

q: PLA which is made from fermented plant starch (usually ____), is now being used as a biodegradable alternative to petroleum-based plastics.
e: PLA which is made from fermented plant starch (usually corn), is now being used as a biodegradable alternative to petroleum-based plastics. Biodegradable plastics can be broken down by microorganisms.

q: Polymer chains also have been designed that incorporate carbonyl groups (C=O) at intervals down their length to make ____ plastics.
e: Polymer chains also have been designed that incorporate carbonyl groups (C=O) at intervals down their length to make photodegradable plastics. Photodegradable plastics slowly break down in light.

q: Many of the things in the environment are made up of ____.
e: Many of the things in the environment are made up of macromolecules. Macromolecules is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The biologically important proteins and nucleic acids are made up of ____ units.
e: The biologically important proteins and nucleic acids are made up of macromolecular units. Macromolecular is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Some of the synthetic macromolecules produced by industries are plastics, resins, nylon, and ____.
e: Some of the synthetic macromolecules produced by industries are plastics, resins, nylon, and rubber. Rubber is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A polymer which consists of more than one kind of monomers is called a ____.
e: A polymer which consists of more than one kind of monomers is called a copolymer. A copolymer is built from two or more different monomers.

q: Polymers are either found in nature or produced in a ____.
e: Polymers are either found in nature or produced in a laboratory. Laboratory is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Based on the kinds of reactions involved, polymerisation is divided into two groups known as addition polymerisation and ____ polymerisation.
e: Based on the kinds of reactions involved, polymerisation is divided into two groups known as addition polymerisation and condensation polymerisation. Condensation joins molecules and knocks out water or another small molecule.

q: The letter "n" in the formula of a polymer represents a large ____.
e: The letter "n" in the formula of a polymer represents a large number. A polymer is a giant molecule made by linking many small monomer units.

q: Polyvinyl chloride's strong, lightweight and durable characteristics make it ideal for pipes, raincoats, thin gloves and flooring ____.
e: Polyvinyl chloride's strong, lightweight and durable characteristics make it ideal for pipes, raincoats, thin gloves and flooring mats. Mats is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Polystyrene (also known as styrofoam) is used to make disposable ____.
e: Polystyrene (also known as styrofoam) is used to make disposable containers. Containers is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The presence of these two different functional groups is required within the same molecule or in two different ____ for condensation polymerisation.
e: The presence of these two different functional groups is required within the same molecule or in two different molecules for condensation polymerisation. Condensation polymerisation joins monomers and knocks out a small molecule such as water.

q: The two monomers for Terylene are represented as a dicarboxylic acid and a ____.
e: The two monomers for Terylene are represented as a dicarboxylic acid and a diol. Diol is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The monomers in polyester are joined together by the ____ linkage.
e: The monomers in polyester are joined together by the ester linkage. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: Nylon is the first synthetic fibre made from a dicarboxylic acid and a ____.
e: Nylon is the first synthetic fibre made from a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine. Diamine is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In the reaction to form nylon, a water molecule is produced from each pair of ____.
e: In the reaction to form nylon, a water molecule is produced from each pair of monomers. Monomers are the small repeating starting molecules of a polymer.

q: Amino acids contain carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen, and some contain ____.
e: Amino acids contain carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen, and some contain sulphur. Sulphur is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Each amino acid differs in terms of its ____ group.
e: Each amino acid differs in terms of its -R group. -R is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Additional amino acids can then react to form a tripeptide, a tetrapeptide, and so on, eventually forming a ____.
e: Additional amino acids can then react to form a tripeptide, a tetrapeptide, and so on, eventually forming a polypeptide. Polypeptide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: An amino acid unit within a polypeptide chain is called an amino acid ____.
e: An amino acid unit within a polypeptide chain is called an amino acid residue. Residue is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The presence of polar functional groups on the chains often enhances chain-chain attractions, and thus, crystallinity and tensile strength ____.
e: The presence of polar functional groups on the chains often enhances chain-chain attractions, and thus, crystallinity and tensile strength increase. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: In the home, polyesters are used to make clothing, carpets, curtains, sheets and ____.
e: In the home, polyesters are used to make clothing, carpets, curtains, sheets and pillows. Pillows is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Increasingly, plastics can be used in place of natural materials such as wood, metal, cotton, and ____.
e: Increasingly, plastics can be used in place of natural materials such as wood, metal, cotton, and leather. Leather is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: As rapidly increasing production and use of disposable plastic products, plastic pollution has become one of the most pressing ____ issues.
e: As rapidly increasing production and use of disposable plastic products, plastic pollution has become one of the most pressing environmental issues. Environmental is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Plastics are mostly flammable; upon incineration, they produce poisonous ____.
e: Plastics are mostly flammable; upon incineration, they produce poisonous gases. Gases is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Plastics may clog up rivers and drains, increasing the flooding in the area and serving as a breeding ground for bacteria and germs that spread ____.
e: Plastics may clog up rivers and drains, increasing the flooding in the area and serving as a breeding ground for bacteria and germs that spread disease. Disease is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: These recycling symbols consist of three arrows around one of seven ____.
e: These recycling symbols consist of three arrows around one of seven numbers. Numbers is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: V/PVC stands for polyvinyl ____.
e: V/PVC stands for polyvinyl chloride. Chloride is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: LDPE stands for low-density ____.
e: LDPE stands for low-density polyethylene. Polyethylene is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: PP stands for ____.
e: PP stands for polypropylene. Polypropylene is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: PS stands for ____.
e: PS stands for polystyrene. Polystyrene is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Some plastics, when buried for many years, eventually become brittle and break down into smaller pieces that can be decomposed naturally by microorganisms in the ____.
e: Some plastics, when buried for many years, eventually become brittle and break down into smaller pieces that can be decomposed naturally by microorganisms in the soil. Soil is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The smaller pieces of plastics have larger surface areas, and hence, it could degrade much more quickly when it is buried in ____.
e: The smaller pieces of plastics have larger surface areas, and hence, it could degrade much more quickly when it is buried in soil. A larger surface area gives more places to collide, so a powdered solid usually reacts faster than a lump.

q: To degrade plastics naturally by microorganisms (bacteria and fungi), plastics should contain small amounts of starch ____.
e: To degrade plastics naturally by microorganisms (bacteria and fungi), plastics should contain small amounts of starch granules. Granules is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Photodegradable plastics incorporate carbonyl groups at intervals down their length to absorb energy from the ultraviolet rays of ____.
e: Photodegradable plastics incorporate carbonyl groups at intervals down their length to absorb energy from the ultraviolet rays of sunlight. Photodegradable plastics slowly break down in light.
